keywords.indexterm: License serverLicensing events in XML format

body.p: The license server also reports individual licensing events at http://hostName:port/oXygenLicenseServlet/license-events. Each event shows which user was granted, rejected, released, or timed out a license, when this happened, and from which computer.

Use this report to see who was denied a license and how often. For example, it can help you determine whether a single user retried many times or whether several different users were affected. The XML report reports only the total number of rejected requests, as a single counter.
body.note: The report does not include license rejections that happen because the user was deactivated in the Users Management page, or because the user is missing from the allowed users list.
This report is protected in the same way as the other license server management pages. You must use a user configured with the admin role, or with the manager role if you configured one.

section.title: Query Parameters

table.title: Parameters of the Licensing Events Report

row.entry: The type of the events to report: rejected, granted, released, timeout, or all.
Reports only events recorded at or after this time.
Reports only events recorded before this time.
Reports only the events that follow the event with this identifier. Use it to read the next page of a truncated report. It cannot be combined with groupBy.
Set it to user to report one row per user instead of one row per event.
The maximum number of rows to report. It must be at least 1, and values larger than 10000 are reduced to 10000.

section.p: The since and until parameters accept either a number of milliseconds since the Unix epoch (1755162723000) or a date in the ISO-8601 format (2026-08-14T09:12:03Z).

section.title: Reported Events
section.p: For example, if the current moment is 14 August 2026, 09:00 UTC, the following request reports users who were denied a license in the last day: /license-events?since=2026-08-13T09:00:00Z:<licenseEvents type="rejected" returned="2" hasMore="true" oldest="2026-02-11T08:00:01Z" nextAfter="10230"> <event id="10229" time="2026-08-14T09:12:03Z" type="rejected" user="jdoe" hostname="jdoe-mbp" ip="10.1.2.3" mac="00:11:22:33:44:55" sessionId="node01ab7x9k2m" usedLicenses="50"/> <event id="10230" time="2026-08-14T09:12:04Z" type="rejected" user="asmith" hostname="asmith-pc" ip="10.1.2.9" mac="00:11:22:33:44:66" sessionId="node01qq2z8p4d" usedLicenses="50"/> </licenseEvents>

The licenseEvents element shows the query result:
returned - The number of reported rows.
hasMore - Whether more events match the query than were reported. When the events are grouped by user, it reports whether more users were left out.
nextAfter - The value to pass as the after parameter to read the next page. It is missing when no event was reported.
oldest - The moment of the oldest event of this type that the license server still has. It is missing when it has none. This lets you distinguish an interval in which nothing happened from an interval that is older than the recorded history.

Each event element reports the identifier and moment of the event, its type, the user name, the host name, the IP address, and the MAC address of the computer where Oxygen runs, the identifier of the session, and the number of licenses that were in use when the event was recorded. Attributes that the license server does not know are omitted rather than left empty. For example, events recorded by a license server older than version 29 have no sessionId.

The user attribute is the only one that is always present. When the client did not specify the user for whom it requested a license, the event is reported for the user (unknown-name), and the events of all such clients are counted together. For events recorded by a license server older than version 29, it is the word user followed by the internal identifier of the user, because the name itself was not recorded at that time.
section.note: The server never merges events, and each event has an identifier larger than the identifiers of the events before it. To follow the events from a monitoring script, store the nextAfter value of a report and pass it as the after parameter of the next request. This way, each event is reported to you exactly once.

section.title: Events Grouped by User
section.p: The groupBy=user parameter counts each user's events instead of reporting them one by one, with the users who have the most events listed first:<licenseEvents type="rejected" groupBy="user" returned="2" hasMore="false" oldest="2026-02-11T08:00:01Z"> <group user="jdoe" count="37"/> <group user="asmith" count="4"/> </licenseEvents>

In the example above, a single user accounts for 37 of the 41 denials, so the license server was most likely short of licenses for one person who retried, rather than for the whole team. The type, since, and until parameters select the events before they are counted, and limit caps the number of reported users.

ul.li: Events are reported only after a license key is activated on the license server, and only the events of the currently active type of license key are reported.
All recorded events are removed when the kind of the activated license key changes.

On a license server that uses a named-user license key, a user's events are also removed together with the user itself, that is when the Oxygen application reports that it did not use the license that it was granted, or when the user is no longer allowed to request a license. A floating license server never removes them.
